title: Northstar: a small customer's migration
disclosure: Synthetic interview — fictional company and speaker

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: How did your small Northstar deployment migrate?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: Our small deployment moved in six weeks because we used only standard connectors.

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: We had twelve users and did not maintain custom integrations. This was one migration, not a representative survey.

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: I cannot estimate how an enterprise deployment would compare.

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: Could you walk me through the sequence of steps you followed during the migration?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: Certainly. We started by auditing all existing workflows to identify which were active and which could be retired. Then we mapped out the data flows using the standard connectors supported by Northstar. After that, we scheduled a phased migration to avoid downtime, moving workflows one by one over a six-week period. Throughout, we tested each workflow in a sandbox environment before going live.

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: Did you encounter any challenges or unexpected issues during this process?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: We did face a few minor hiccups. For example, one connector behaved slightly differently in the new system, which required us to adjust some workflow logic. Also, our email notifications needed reconfiguration due to changes in authentication protocols. However, none of these issues caused significant delays.

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: How did you manage communication and handoffs between teams during the migration?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: Since our team was small, communication was informal but consistent. We used a shared project board to track progress and issues. Whenever a workflow was ready for migration, the developer responsible would notify the rest of the team for review and testing. This approach worked well for us but might be insufficient for larger deployments.

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: Were there any workarounds you had to implement due to limitations in the migration tools?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: Yes, we noticed that the migration tool didn't fully support some conditional logic in older workflows. To handle this, we manually recreated those parts post-migration. It was a bit tedious but manageable given our small scale.

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: Did you observe any differences in performance or user experience after the migration?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: Performance was generally stable, with some workflows executing slightly faster. Users appreciated the cleaner interface and found the system more intuitive. However, since we had a limited number of users, these observations might not translate to larger organizations.

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: Looking back, is there anything you would do differently if you had to repeat this migration?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: I would allocate more time upfront for training and documentation. While the migration itself was smooth, some users struggled initially with new features. Also, involving end-users earlier in testing could have helped identify minor issues sooner.
